question: Which of the following is NOT an alkaline solution?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Aluminum hydroxide**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Aluminum Hydroxide (Al(OH)₃)**:

 
 
• Aluminum hydroxide is not considered a strong alkaline solution.
 
• While it can act as a base, it is amphoteric, meaning it can react with both acids and bases.
 
• In aqueous solution, it does not produce a significant concentration of hydroxide ions compared to strong bases.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sodium Hydroxide (NaOH)**:

 
 
• Sodium hydroxide is a strong base and is commonly used as an alkaline solution in various industrial and laboratory applications.
 
• It fully dissociates in water to produce hydroxide ions (OH⁻).
 
 
 
• **Magnesium Hydroxide (Mg(OH)₂)**:
 
 
• Magnesium hydroxide is also a strong base and is used in antacids and as a laxative.
 
 
• It partially dissociates in water but still provides alkaline properties.
 
 
 
 
 
• **Calcium Hydroxide (Ca(OH)₂):**
 
 
• Calcium hydroxide, also known as slaked lime, is a strong base that is used in various applications, including construction and agriculture.
 
• It dissociates in water to produce hydroxide ions.
